newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Mark/Swiss franc capped just above 85.12.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Mark/Swiss franc capped just above 85.12.

text.p: The Swiss franc was trundling sideways against the mark in Europe, capped just above 85.12 and supported at 84.90 centimes, said analysts.
"The market is very sluggish at the moment," said Joachim Goldberg, Frankfurt-based global head of technical analysis at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
He said while longer-term the odds favour the upside for mark/Swiss, an advance would eventually be capped around the 85.60/90 level.
He said a stumble below the 84.85/90 area would meet fresh support at 84.45/05 centimes.
At 0858 GMT mark/Swiss Franc was trading at 85.11/15 against 85.12 centimes in late Europe on Friday.
While dollar/Swiss franc edged higher on Monday, analysts said a closing break of 1.4760 was needed to confirm the upside - though this was seen as unlikely.
"Dollar/Swiss is still range trading and could break both ways. Medium-term limits are 1.4400 and 1.4830," said Dominique Corombelle, technical analyst at Generale Bank in Brussels.
He said a break of 1.4650 support should be watched, with a slip below 1.4610 confirming a downwards move down to 1.4400.
RSI - 14 day: Dlr/Swiss: 54 pct, Mark/Swiss: 43 pct -- Julia Meehan, London forex desk, +44 171 542 6701
